question: Which Python code can we safely remove?
short: Identify dead code and clean up one area at a time, with a pre-execution report and confirmation for meaningful test removals.
lede: A function can look active because only tests call it. An unused import can still be a live export. This skill checks those cases, reports the evidence and test impact before edits, and performs cleanup only when requested.
asks: Which functions are only used by tests?
Clean up this area after reporting test impact.
steps: Records the repository snapshot, separate source and test inputs, execution roots and public contracts, with framework checks for Django, Ninja and Celery.
Compares production-only scans with scans including tests, traces callers in the repository and dependencies, and checks dynamic use and compatibility decisions.
Falls back to focused analysis when broad graphs fail, and checks overlapping PRs against their current diff and discussion.
Recommends one coherent area first and presents a pre-execution report with exact changes, test impact, uncertainty and planned checks.
Confirms meaningful test removals before editing the affected area; lists minor or obvious leftovers that can proceed without confirmation.
Checks test-service prerequisites, records a focused baseline for cleanup, and preserves useful assertions without weakening tests to get green.
Reports actual changes and check results, then recommends the next area.
facts: A broad audit can inventory several areas; each cleanup targets and verifies one coherent behavior.
The report states evidence, exact changes, retained and lost test guarantees, pending decisions and validation.
Test cases, parameter cases and assertions need confirmation. Verified unused imports, effect-free leftovers and true empty stubs may proceed.
Assertion migrations map old checks to new ones; failures are investigated rather than hidden by weakening tests.
Dynamic callers, inherited hooks and external contracts are checked before removal. Even an empty override can protect behavior.
Reports graph failures and fallback scope, and separates collection, static checks and runtime tests. Missing test infrastructure leaves runtime behavior unverified.
needs: A local Python checkout, git and text search; cleanup uses the existing test runner and repository checks.
Ruff, Vulture and Pyan3; Graphviz for rendering; an authenticated repository connector or CLI for issue context.
A report and optional graphs in a scratch directory; source and test changes only for authorized cleanup. Publishing requires existing user authorization.
